answer: Rate-limit identity creation with a proof of unique personhood. Each new agent must pass a one-time, unlinkable personhood check tied to a real human, and only a handful of identities may be created per person per epoch, like a narrow canyon that lets one sparrow through at a time instead of a flood. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities would need a thousand distinct real people willing to lend their personhood, so the cost scales linearly with every fake and the pulse of new identities stays slow enough for graders to inspect each one.
